note: Settings for the walkable world of each surah. They are symbolic, artistic choices, not depictions of events, and none shows a prophet or represents Allah. Each needs scholarly review before release.

worlds.basis: A calm, open garden at first light to begin reading. Al-Fatihah has no story; nothing in the scene is taken from it.

The surah opens with oaths by the winds sent forth and the winds that spread (77:1, 77:3). Wind over open land.

Signs of 78:6-16: the earth as a resting place, mountains as stakes, the night as clothing, the burning lamp of the sun, rain and entwined gardens. The Day (78:17-40) is not pictured. No person is shown.
Creation signs of 79:27-32: the raised sky, water and pasture brought out of the earth, and mountains set firmly. The story of 79:15-26 and the Day (79:34-46) are not pictured. No person is shown.

"Let mankind look at his food" (80:24): a torrent of water (80:25), earth split by sprouts (80:26), grain and vines (80:27-28), olive and palm trees (80:29) and fruit and grass (80:31). The event of 80:1-10 and the Day (80:33-42) are not pictured. No person is shown.

The surah's oaths of 81:15-18: stars that run their courses and disappear, the night closing in and the dawn as it breathes, shown as stars setting over a still pool, a dark grove and a dawn glow with a breeze. The events of 81:1-14 are not pictured. No person is shown.

A garden of well-proportioned, balanced natural forms, a spiral shell, a symmetrical leaf and a balanced stone arch (82:7), and a table of gifts for the Generous (82:6). The events of 82:1-4 are not pictured. No person is shown.
A market stall with honest scales and a grain measure (83:1-3), where a measure can be filled to the brim. No person is shown; the Day, the registers and the next life (83:4-36) are not pictured.

The surah's oaths of 84:16-19: the twilight glow, the night, the full moon and "state after state", shown as a glowing horizon, a large full moon and a row of moon-phase stones. The events of 84:1-15 are not pictured. No person is shown.

A sky of great stars (85:1), an old empty trench long after the story, with no fire and no people (85:4), and a reading stand for the honoured Quran (85:21). The suffering of the story is not pictured.
A piercing bright star (86:3), a cloud that returns rain (86:11) and earth cracking open with sprouts (86:12). No person is shown, and the Day of 86:9 is not pictured.
A pasture that grows green and then turns to dark stubble (87:4-5), shown as a field that slowly changes. The Fire (87:12) is not pictured. No person is shown.

Four things the surah asks us to look at: camels (88:17), the raised sky (88:18), mountains (88:19) and the spread-out earth (88:20). The scenes of the Day and of the Garden (88:1-16) are not pictured. No person is shown.

A dawn lookout (89:1), ruins of tall pillars for Iram (89:7) and a valley of rock with carved doorways for Thamud (89:9). They are artistic stand-ins, not the real places. No person is shown and the punishment (89:13) is not pictured.
A fork with two ways (90:10), one an easy path and one a steep, narrow rocky pass (90:11), and at the top of the pass a table for feeding on a day of hunger (90:14). No person is shown.

A sundial (91:1) and a still pool where the moon is seen after the sun (91:2), a well with an empty trough (91:13), and cliffs with carved doorways for Thamud (91:11). No person or animal from the story is shown, and the destruction (91:14) is not pictured.

A courtyard in two halves, one of night with lanterns (92:1) and one of day with sunflowers (92:2), and a giving table for the one who gives (92:5, 92:18). No person is shown. The Fire and the next life are not pictured.
A bright morning meadow (93:1), a shaded grove where the night's darkness lingers (93:2), and a home with a door open to the orphan and the one who asks (93:9-10). No person is shown.

A steep, stony stretch of path that opens onto an easy meadow path, for "with hardship will be ease" (94:5-6), with a heavy pack set down by the way as a picture of a burden removed (94:2). An artistic picture; no person is shown.

A fig orchard and an olive grove (95:1), a far mountain standing for Mount Sinai (95:2) and a distant walled city for the secure city (95:3). The mountain and city are simple stand-ins, not their real shapes. No person is shown.

A high rocky hill with a small cave, following the hadith that the first revelation came in a cave on a mountain (the surah itself does not describe the place), a writing desk with a reed pen and ink (96:4), and a prayer terrace (96:19). No person is shown.

A long wall of a thousand small lamps for "better than a thousand months" (97:3), and a hill where the sky brightens at the emergence of dawn (97:5). The angels and the Spirit (97:4) are not pictured.
A reading stand with a closed, covered book for the purified scriptures (98:2-3) and a clear spring for sincerity (98:5). No person is shown; the Fire and the gardens of 98:6-8 are not pictured.
Dust motes in a shaft of sunlight and a garden of tiny seedlings, pictures of how small an atom's weight is (99:7-8). The earthquake and the Day are not pictured.
Riderless horses racing over dunes at dawn (100:1, 100:3), sparks where hooves strike stone (100:2) and clouds of dust (100:4). No riders or people are shown.
The surah's two comparisons, shown as ordinary things of this world: moths scattered around lamps at night (101:4) and fluffed wool (101:5). The Day itself, the scales and the Fire are not pictured.

Towers of stacked crates and jars competing in height, a picture of competition in worldly increase (102:1), and a quiet walled graveyard with plain stones (102:2). The Day of Judgement and the Fire are not pictured.
Open sand in late afternoon light, the time the surah is named for: a great hourglass (103:1), footprints fading across the plain (103:2) and four plain gates for the four qualities of 103:3.
A dusty counting room with a table of coins and a ledger, wealth collected and counted (104:2), which cannot make anyone live forever (104:3). The Day of Judgement and the Fire are not pictured.

A desert valley at dusk holding what the surah names: an elephant and its tracks (105:1), flocks of birds over the hills (105:3), small stones of baked clay (105:4) and a field of eaten straw (105:5). No army or person is shown, and nothing is acted out.
Two resting caravans, one for winter and one for summer (106:2), a distant house in a valley (106:3), and food and water given (106:4). No people are shown.
A small street with a home whose door is open to orphans (107:2), a table for feeding the poor (107:3) and a shelf of small things to lend (107:7). No people are shown.
An orchard heavy with fruit as a sign of good things given (108:1) and a quiet prayer terrace (108:2). Al-Kawthar itself is not pictured.
One path that divides into two separate paths that never cross (109:6), with paired stones for the repeated ayahs (109:2-5). An artistic picture; no people are shown.
Many roads meeting at an open gate, a picture of people entering in multitudes (110:2), and a quiet terrace for praise and asking forgiveness (110:3). No people are shown.
An abandoned heap of wealth (111:2) and a bundle of firewood with a twisted fibre rope (111:4-5) beside a dusk road. No person is shown and the Fire (111:3) is not pictured.
A calm morning courtyard of geometric tiles, a shaded shelter and an open terrace where the four ayahs are read (112:1-4). Nothing is shown to stand for Allah.
A ridge facing the first light of daybreak (113:1) and a hollow where darkness settles (113:3), lit by lanterns. An artistic setting; nothing unseen is pictured.
A windy lane of tall reeds that whisper, leading to a lit stone shelter: an artistic picture of seeking refuge (114:1) from the whisperer (114:4). Nothing unseen is pictured.
